summary: Resubmission sub-muz4pt2i-01b2f7f7 resolves VER-1 via resolution (a). I checked the hash-chained log myself: RISK-12 was re-recorded with status 'accepted' by actor 'user' (seq 520), and decisions dec-muz4ocip-016d36bd and dec-muz4ocl7-01aaa32d were recorded by actor 'user' (seq 521, 522), before the resubmission (seq 524). The first decision explicitly accepts the 0.571 (n=7) vs 0.70 holdout miss and amends SC2/AC8 for this release only. The chain, content hashes and snapshot replay all verify (ev:ev-muz4st62-0172d9be). The report and checklist cite the decision accurately and change no result: 24/25, holdout high_urgency_recall 0.571 n=7 still FAIL, full-mode run count 1. These match the untampered first-full-eval log (ev:ev-muz4rtv1-01c429a3, ev:ev-muz4sgqs-013dd869). There is still exactly one full-mode eval record. The eval inputs still match the freeze hashes. I re-ran npm test: 439/439 pass (ev:ev-muz4s14h-011bf384). Two of my own probes failed, and the failures are my errors, not the submission's: ev-muz4rtxg-016135f8 hashed the eval log file including the engine's 3-line header, and the engine hashes only the output body (corrected in ev-muz4sgqs-013dd869). ev-muz4rtnu-01eba046 ran the CLI 'audit', which also flags report.md and release-checklist.md as changed since the phase:integration approval. That flag is expected: these two files are re-reviewed artifacts of this gate, and approving this gate makes their latest approved hash the current one. The hash-chain part of the audit passes (ev-muz4st62-0172d9be).

findings.title: The event log cannot prove that 'actor: user' was a human
findings.detail: Events 520-522 carry actor 'user', and the hash chain verifies (ev:ev-muz4st62-0172d9be). However, the CLI accepts '--actor user' from any caller. The events fall between run-muyrc542 (ended 23:49:54) and run-muz4oqf9 (started 06:01:08), so no agent run was open when they were written. That timing is consistent with a direct user action. Even so, the log alone cannot prove human authorship.
findings.recommendation: Orchestrator: confirm with the user in the delivery handoff that they personally made dec-muz4ocip-016d36bd. Engine improvement: authenticate or attest the 'user' actor.

findings.title: Fallback holdout high-urgency recall miss carried forward as accepted risk
findings.detail: Holdout high_urgency_recall stays at 0.571 (4/7) and held-out-family injection flag recall at 0.444. This release accepts them under RISK-12 and dec-muz4ocip-016d36bd. The decision defers the alternative: a rules revision validated on a fresh holdout.
findings.recommendation: Next release: revise t11 rules on tune rows only and validate against a new, unseen holdout frozen before the change.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Resolution (a) is met. The user recorded RISK-12 as 'accepted' (seq 520, actor user) and decision dec-muz4ocip-016d36bd (seq 521, actor user). The decision accepts the fallback holdout high_urgency_recall of 0.571 (n=7) against the 0.70 floor as a known limitation and amends SC2/AC8 for this release only, with the fallback stated to be a labelled safety net. The hash chain verifies, and both records precede resubmission sub-muz4pt2i-01b2f7f7 (seq 524). The report and checklist cite the decision in the section 'User decision on RISK-12 (2026-10-08)'. Results are unchanged: 24/25, 0.571 n=7 still reported as FAIL, full-mode run count 1, matching the untampered first-full-eval log. No second full-mode run exists, eval inputs match the freeze, and npm test passes 439/439.
